seoTitle: How to Copy Google Gemini Responses Into Word (2026)
metaDescription: Move a Gemini response into Microsoft Word with its headings and lists intact: use the copy icon, pick the right Word paste option, or go via Export to Docs and download a .docx.
intro:
Gemini has no Export to Word button. There are two clean ways to get a response into a Word document anyway. For a section or two, copy it with the icon under the response and paste it into Word. For a long report, send it to Google Docs with Gemini's Export to Docs option and download that as a .docx.

The copy is quick. What decides whether the result looks right is the paste option you pick in Word, because Word's default keeps Gemini's own fonts and spacing instead of your document's. This guide covers both routes and the paste choice.

steps.heading: Ask for the structure you want in Word
steps.body: Go to gemini.google.com and write your prompt. If the text is headed for a Word document, say so in the prompt: ask for headings, numbered sections or a table. Structure Gemini produces comes across as real headings and lists. Structure you add afterwards is manual work in Word.

image.caption: Gemini's starting screen with the prompt box ready.

steps.heading: Copy the finished response with the copy icon
steps.body:
Wait until Gemini has stopped writing. The row of icons under the response (thumbs up, thumbs down, regenerate, copy and a three-dot menu) appears once it's done, and copying earlier can cut off the last sections.

Click the copy icon. It takes the whole response in one go, formatting included. Dragging to select a long answer by hand tends to miss the first or last line, or pick up the suggested follow-up prompts underneath.

image.caption: The end of a long Gemini response with the action row underneath: thumbs up, thumbs down, regenerate, copy and more.

steps.heading: Paste into Word and choose a paste option
steps.body:
Put your cursor in the Word document and press Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on a Mac). By default Word keeps the source formatting, so the text arrives in Gemini's fonts and spacing.

If that clashes with your document, click the Paste Options button that appears beside the pasted text, or press Ctrl straight after pasting, and pick one of the options in the table below. Merge Formatting is usually the right call for a document that already has its own look.

If you do this often, set the default under File > Options > Advanced > Cut, copy, and paste, using the Pasting from other programs setting.

steps.heading: Tidy headings with Word's styles
steps.body: Scroll through once. Check that numbered lists kept their numbers, that headings still stand out, and that nested points kept their indent. Where a heading came through as plain bold text, click into it and apply Heading 1 or Heading 2 from the Home tab. Using styles, instead of setting font sizes by hand, keeps the section in step with the rest of the document and makes it show up in a table of contents.

steps.heading: For long responses, export to Docs and download a .docx
steps.body:
Under the response, choose Share & export, then Export to Docs. If you don't see Share & export as its own button, check the three-dot menu at the end of the action row. Gemini saves the response as a new Google Doc in your Drive.

Open that doc and go to File > Download > Microsoft Word (.docx). You get a Word file with the headings and lists already in place, which beats pasting a long report in pieces. Tables have their own route too: Export to Sheets at the bottom right of a table saves it to a new spreadsheet, as long as the table contains no images.

tables.note: Option names from Microsoft's Word support documentation for Word for Microsoft 365 and Word 2016 to 2024.

troubleshooting.problem: Pasted text is in a different font and size from the rest of the document
troubleshooting.cause: Word's default paste keeps source formatting, so Gemini's styling comes along with the text.
troubleshooting.fix: Undo, paste again and choose Merge Formatting from the Paste Options button. To stop it happening, change Pasting from other programs under File > Options > Advanced.

troubleshooting.problem: A table from Gemini disappeared after pasting
troubleshooting.cause: Keep Text Only discards tables and other non-text elements.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste again with Keep Source Formatting or Merge Formatting, or use Export to Sheets on the table in Gemini.

troubleshooting.problem: Share & export or Export to Docs isn't there
troubleshooting.cause: On a Google Workspace (work or school) account, which export options you get depends on availability and your organisation's settings.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the copy icon and paste route instead, or ask your Workspace admin whether Gemini exports are turned on.

faq.question: Can Gemini export straight to a Word file?
faq.answer: Not directly. Gemini exports to Google Docs. From there, File > Download > Microsoft Word (.docx) gives you a Word file.

faq.question: Why does pasted Gemini text look different from my document?
faq.answer: Word keeps the source formatting by default. Choose Merge Formatting from the Paste Options button to make the text take on your document's styles.

faq.question: Can I get a Gemini table into Excel?
faq.answer: Use Export to Sheets at the bottom right of the table, then download the sheet as an Excel file. Tables that contain images can't be exported to Sheets.

verifiedNote: Gemini screens and the copy icon's position come from the original screen recording. Gemini's export options and Word's paste options were re-checked against Google's Gemini Apps Help and Microsoft's Word support documentation in September 2026. That check added the Export to Docs route and corrected the paste advice: Word's option for adopting the document's look is Merge Formatting, not "Match destination formatting" as this guide previously said.
